title: Closed models [notes postérieures à PS ?] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. A and B are small categories and A^, B^, (A×B)^ are their presheaf categories. p_A : A×B → B is the projection, so p_A^*(M) is a presheaf M on B pulled back to A×B. For X, Y in (A×B)^, Hom_B(X,Y) is the relative internal Hom: a presheaf on B with sections over b given by morphisms over B/b, i.e. Hom(X×p^*(b), Y). Y^M is the relative exponential.

The page opens with the topos-theoretic adjunction Hom_B(X, Y^M) ≅ Hom_B(X×p_A^*M, Y). This holds for all presheaves X, Y on A×B.

Grothendieck's interest is the full subcategory Hom(B°,A) ⊂ (A×B)^. These are presheaves X with each X(b) := X(-,b) representable, i.e. 'B-objects of A' (simplicial objects in A when B = Δ). He wants the cotensor Y^M and the tensor X⊗M to stay inside Hom(B°,A).

- For Y^M this was settled on earlier pages. It needs certain projective limits in A, but not internal Homs in A.
- For the tensor, X×p_A^*M is b ↦ X(b)×M(b) = ∐^{A^}_{σ∈M(b)} X(b). This is a coproduct taken in presheaves, so it is generally not representable.
- If A has coproducts (finite ones suffice when the M(b) are finite sets), he sets (X⊗M)(b) := ∐^A_{σ∈M(b)} X(b), the copower of X(b) by the set M(b), computed in A.
- There is a canonical comparison between the presheaf coproduct and the representable of the A-coproduct, which is not an isomorphism.
- Since Y takes representable values, every map from the presheaf coproduct into Y(b) factors uniquely through the A-coproduct. Hence Hom_B(X, Y^M) ≅ Hom_B(X⊗M, Y) for X, Y in Hom(B°,A), as he says 'trivialement'.

Purpose. This makes Hom(B°,A) tensored and cotensored, fibrewise over B^, with Hom_B as the B^-valued Hom. For B = Δ it is exactly Quillen's simplicial structure on simplicial objects of a category with finite limits and colimits, where (X⊗K)_n = ∐_{K_n} X_n. Grothendieck is generalizing it to an arbitrary indexing category B, presumably a test category, in view of closed model structures (an SM7-type axiom) on B-objects in A.
errors: Minor: the comparison map between the coproduct in A^ and the (Yoneda image of the) coproduct in A runs from the A^-coproduct to the representable of the A-coproduct: ∐^{A^} h_{X(b)} → h_{∐^A X(b)}. The page's notation for this arrow, annotated 'non i[so]', is ambiguous about direction; read with the correct direction the argument is sound.
Implicit point: the isomorphism must hold naturally over B/b, not just objectwise. It does, because restriction along B/b → B commutes with the pointwise copower construction.

ideas.what: Relative exponential adjunction Hom_B(X,Y^M) ≅ Hom_B(X×p^*M, Y) in the presheaf topos (A×B)^ viewed over B^
ideas.modern_name: Cartesian closedness of a presheaf topos, relative to the base B^ (internal Hom over a base)
ideas.where_published: SGA 4 (internal Hom in topoi); used throughout Pursuing Stacks

ideas.what: Tensoring of B-objects of A by presheaves on B via pointwise copowers, (X⊗M)(b) = ∐_{M(b)} X(b), adjoint to the cotensor Y^M
ideas.modern_name: Pointwise tensoring/cotensoring of the functor category A^{B°} over B^, generalizing Quillen's simplicial structure on sC
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quillen, Homotopical Algebra (1967), Ch. II §1 for B = Δ; general enriched category theory (Kelly) for the general case
ideas.where_published: Possibly related passages in Pursuing Stacks / Les Dérivateurs; not verified

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine verification. It extends Quillen's well-known simplicial tensoring/cotensoring of simplicial objects to B-objects for an arbitrary B, and it is mathematically standard. It shows Grothendieck's working context of model structures on 'B-objects' (B a test category), but contains nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'Hom_A(a, X(b))' is the value at a of the presheaf represented by X(b), written by abuse of notation; the struck-through text before it is 'Hom' started then rewritten.
'il n'est pas toujours représentable' should more likely read 'il n'est pas en général représentable' (meaning unchanged).
The parenthetical arrow annotated 'non iso' compares ∐^A X(b) with ∐^{A^}_{σ∈M(b)} X(b) = (X×p_A^*(M))(b); the natural direction is from the A^-coproduct to the A-coproduct.
'pour X, Y dans Hom(B°; A)': the struck-through character before X is a deleted subscript, not part of the formula.
